title: asymmetric-prefill-decode-scheduler-with-lazy-kv-priming
author: Diego Ramos
release_notes: Introduce asymmetric prefill/decode scheduler and lazy KV priming to reduce tail latency and improve throughput for mixed short/long request workloads. Backwards-compatible runtime changes; opt-in via config flag.
description: Motivation: In mixed workloads with a heavy tail of long generations, symmetric prefill/decode handoff causes prefill work to stall short requests and permits decode kernels to contend for KV cache bandwidth. This PR introduces an asymmetric orchestration scheme: 1) prefill scheduling is split into light and heavy lanes, 2) decode stages can preempt long prefill chunks after a configurable handoff threshold, and 3) a lazy KV priming mechanism warms KV pages only for the light-lane prefill window and asynchronously for the heavy-lane in the background. Design summary: add an AsymmetricCoordinator that maintains two token pools (light/heavy), integrate a preemptible chunk scheduler to allow low-latency decodes to 'steal' GPU dispatch slots, implement lazy_kv_priming that does incremental KV page touch and a compact priming metadata structure to avoid full KV scans at dispatch time. Backwards-compatibility: new behavior is guarded by runtime config flags (scheduling.asymmetric_enabled, kv.lazy_priming=true) and defaults to previous pipeline. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4021), [x] unit tests for coordinator & priming, [x] integration perf tests, [x] CLI config + console toggles, [x] canary rollout manifest. Commits summary: 1) add asymm coordinator and token pool (core/scheduler) 2) implement preemptible-chunking with handoff threshold heuristics 3) lazy KV priming + priming metadata and GC 4) metrics/hooks and dashboard widgets 5) tests and perf harness updates 6) docs and config defaults. Changed areas: core/scheduler/*, runtime/prefill/*, runtime/decode/*, runtime/kvcache/priming.{cc,h}, observability/metrics_registry, tests/perf/asymmetric_end2end.yaml, docs/running/asymmetric_scheduler.md. Benchmarks: stable canary on p4d: 14% reduction in p95 latency for short requests under mixed load, 9% increase in overall throughput for the same GPU pool with default priming; heavy-only synthetic load shows <3% throughput regression (expected) when asymmetric is enabled due to background priming overhead. Observability: new metrics prefilling_lane_usage{light|heavy}, kv_priming_bytes, scheduler_preempt_events. Rollout plan: feature off by default; staged rollout with 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> full, monitor prefilling_lane_usage and p95 for short requests. Notes: tuned handoff threshold default to 64 tokens based on internal evaluation; future work includes adaptive thresholding based on workload RTT.
